extracted.intended_audience: early-career scientists and engineers at invited research universities; prospective Packard Fellowship applicants
extracted.subtask_description: Guidelines and program description for the David and Lucile Packard Foundation Fellowships for Science and Engineering, a competitive, institutionally-limited award for early-career university-based researchers. Covers who is selected, award size/duration, and the program's emphasis on flexible, risk-taking research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection pool and number of fellows
rubrics_metrics.description: Each year, the Foundation selects 20 Fellows from 50 invited institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Selection is limited to nominees from a defined set of invited institutions; only 20 awards are made annually.

rubrics_metrics.name: Award amount and duration
rubrics_metrics.description: Individual grants of $875,000, distributed over five years.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fellows receive a single-person grant totaling $875,000 to be paid across a five-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Flexible use of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows can use their funds in whatever way would best advance their research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The program emphasizes flexibility—recipients are not constrained to specific budget line items and may allocate funds according to what will most effectively further their research goals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Early-career status and exceptional promise
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is intended to allow the nation’s most promising early-career scientists and engineers flexible funding to take risks and explore new frontiers in their fields of study.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should be at an early-career stage and demonstrate exceptional promise; the Foundation seeks individuals likely to make significant advances in their fields.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasis on ambitious, risk-taking, and novel research
rubrics_metrics.description: Fellows are encouraged to think big and look at complex issues with a fresh perspective.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship favors research that is ambitious, exploratory, and willing to take risks or pursue unconventional approaches to important problems.

rubrics_metrics.name: University-based affiliation
rubrics_metrics.description: The program is rooted in David Packard’s commitment to strengthening university-based science and engineering programs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The fellowship supports university-based researchers and is structured to strengthen research programs within academic institutions (selection tied to invited institutions).
